A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KaLM-Embedding-V2 work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v3 reports original MTEB evaluations, training-component ablations, industrial retrieval experiments, dimensionality analyses, and case studies.

after.justification: v6 retains those original results and adds English MTEB v2 and seven-language AIR-Bench QA evaluations.

M1.justification: The Qwen2-0.5B backbone, bidirectional attention, mean pooling, focal reweighting, negative mixing, contrastive distillation, and Matryoshka training remain unchanged. The new clarification that MKL uses full-dimensional teacher signals documents an existing component rather than establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: v6 adds AIR-Bench QA evaluation across seven languages, extending the previously English/Chinese evaluation coverage to Spanish, French, Japanese, German, and Russian and introducing automatically generated retrieval scenarios. The training-dataset lists remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 add Qwen3-Embedding-4B and Qwen3-Embedding-8B to the main Chinese comparison; the latter was already a teacher and industrial OOD comparator in v3. New comparisons also introduce multilingual-e5-large-instruct, bge-large-en-v1.5, EmbeddingGemma-300M, and gte-Qwen2-7B-instruct, substantially broadening the evaluated comparison set.

E3.justification: v6 adds a separate 41-task English MTEB v2 evaluation and AIR-Bench QA 24.05 evaluation using NDCG@10 and a specified general retrieval instruction. Existing training budgets, the 512-token evaluation limit, MTEB v1 task exclusions, and industrial retrieval protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds a multilingual/OOD generalization check beyond the main English/Chinese evaluations. Existing component ablations, temperature sensitivity, Matryoshka analyses, HotpotQA cases, and embedding visualizations are retained. The new Figure 4 redisplays existing Table 5 ablation results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its experiments. The retained case-study boxplots summarize hard-negative similarity scores, rather than estimation uncertainty; the new ablation chart adds no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v6 adds substantive benchmark findings: KaLM-Embedding-V2.5 scores 71.29 MTK on English MTEB v2 and 49.02 on AIR-Bench QA, versus 49.33 for gte-Qwen2-7B-instruct. These are newly reported evaluations, not improvements over v3 under identical settings. Existing MTEB v1, industrial OOD, and ablation scores remain unchanged. Table 11 corrects three relative-drop values, including the Chinese 128-dimensional V2.5 drop from -1.607% to -1.650%.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 retain the same embedding definitions, contrastive and focal losses, negative-mixing formulas, KL objective, and instruction formulation. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs; the model-agnostic distillation statement is an applicability claim.

C1.justification: The central contributions and compact-model MTEB performance claims remain. v6's introduction adds the claim of performance comparable to leading multilingual embedding models despite lacking large-scale multilingual training, extending the stated generalization scope.

C2.justification: v6 explicitly describes contrastive distillation as model-agnostic and interprets AIR-Bench results as demonstrating multilingual and low-resource generalization. Its new claim of no large-scale multilingual training is difficult to reconcile with Table 16's large multilingual corpora. Earlier mechanism explanations and dimensionality-related limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v6 replaces the future-release promise with stated code, data, and model availability and supplies project/model access links. It clarifies the STS score range as [0,5], full-dimensional teacher signals for MKL, and the AIR-Bench instruction. Existing hardware counts, training times, hyperparameters, and dataset statistics are retained.

R1.justification: v6 adds references including MMTEB, AIR-Bench, EmbeddingGemma, Jasper and Stella, jina-embeddings-v5-text, and memory-augmented transformers, while refining its description of E5. The central research positioning remains. Consolidated NV-Embed, MTEB, and Sentence-BERT references represent duplicate/publication cleanup rather than removed research.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. v6 makes localized clarifications, updates author affiliations and conference headers, and adds acknowledgments, a reproducibility statement, and an LLM-use appendix. Appendix lettering and cross-references are updated.

P2.justification: v6 adds the four-panel ablation Figure 4 and Tables 12–13, expands Tables 2–3, and relocates Figure 1 while clarifying its color caption. The original performance plots, workflow diagrams, case-study plots, and embedding visualizations are retained without redrawing.

improvement.justification: The added English MTEB v2 and multilingual retrieval evaluations, broader comparisons, MKL clarification, and corrected percentages improve empirical assessment and precision. The gains are limited because the core method and main evidence remain stable. The new multilingual-training claim also conflicts with Table 16's large multilingual entries, weakening that interpretation without negating the usefulness of the added results.
